text: BIS: Stablecoins and Bank Deposits Act as Substitutes as Deposit Hikes Slow Stablecoin Growth BIS (Bank for International Settlements) working paper finds that stablecoins and bank deposits act as direct portfolio substitutes. Analyzing U.S. data, the authors show that a 1-basis-point hike in bank deposit rates cuts 10-week stablecoin market cap growth by roughly 3 percentage points (and up to ~9 percentage points under an IV approach). The substitution effect is significantly stronger for onshore-tied USDC (-4.8%) than offshore-centric USDT (-1.9%) and holds across bank CD rates and DeFi lending yields, demonstrating that traditional bank deposit pricing exerts an active drag on stablecoin growth. — link

text: How to perceive your own intelligence This is a topic I've pondered ever since I was in high school and first started my journey of trying to become rich through the internet. And one that I've recently become more aware of due to having extra social interactions. I saw an interesting video which basically said that locking in on your computer isn't actually that hard in comparison to going out into social settings, dates, dinners, organised sports etc. Since anyone can sit on their computer and it requires little agency (im not saying that our small circle of traders aren't high agency), the harder task is becoming presentable, knowledgable, charismatic etc in a world filed with sheep designed by the social media slop factory. If you were to take the rarity of someone who is a high calibre entrepreneur, AI coder, trader, influencer/course seller vs someone who can control/thrive in a social environment, I think the former would be higher in numbers these days. Since markets have been slower and I had a perspective change from that video I watched, I put my foot forward to force myself into more social dinners and dates. Being internet native for the past several years, my subconscious felt I never really belonged in environments like this due all the excess screen time which gave me an autistic type of persona. I've been quite aware of these feelings I've had for some time now. Lack of gratitude was always something that I've really battled with and I felt like improving this over the past year has been one of my biggest mental unlocks towards life. Now I'm able to sit in the present and be comfortable in my own skin even if things aren't going my way. I can view events more as external things happening around me which don't affect my self worth or perception of myself. I'm not as driven by a specific number but the quality of my overall mood and mental state on a daily basis. This might sound like a weird correlation, but I've felt like my increase in gratitude has reflected very strongly on my overall facial appearance as it's essentially stripping away stress which gets ingrained into your micro expressions/features (when looking back at photos of myself 2 years ago this is apparent). Also my movement patterns of how I walk, posture, vibrancy in conversations, listening skills etc. As I've put myself in more social settings, now instead of having that underlying autistic feeling going into conversations, I feel much more confident, engaged and genuinely interested in how they perceive people or things. So when conversations start opening up, naturally flowing and going beyond surface level, all of the weird quirky things I've learnt over the years become really good sources of stimulation. As I can draw abstract correlations to different fields and also attach some type of data/research to support the idea. Which has allowed me to gauge my own intelligence far better than some type of IQ test. Being able to see the micro expressions of how people respond to your way of thinking or seeing if your ideas are consensus/non consensus among a specific crowd gives you extremely adaptable feedback. Its one thing to read all day long and feed theses into LLM's, but lately I've been really stimulated by deep conversations which get emotional feedback from humans instead of machines. For myself, in certain situations this has been a better analysis of my own intelligence compared to receiving feedback from anonymous people across the internet, as it's much harder to fake ingenuity in face to face scenarios. I'm not discounting the idea and feedback of highly academic/well researched individuals, although it feels like unlocking a new aspect of my character which was once a personality flaw and is now being turned into a strength.
